comparison: Perfect alignment on autonomous vs manual training comparison (C80-C96). Both evaluations support the findings showing trade-offs between training methods, with peer reviewers specifically highlighting this comparison as a strength and finding it 'intriguing'.

Perfect alignment on circadian and temporal behavioral patterns (C108-C119). Both support the findings. Peer Reviewer 2 initially raised concerns about task engagement but later confirmed these were 'adequately addressed' in revision.

Perfect alignment on reversal learning and long-term training capabilities (C120-C123). Both evaluations support the extensive reversal training data, with peer reviewers highlighting 'long-term measurement' as a strength.

Perfect alignment on continuous learning and multi-task training (C135-C140). Both support the findings on learning dynamics, reaction time patterns, and bias patterns, with peer reviewers accepting the data without methodological challenges.

Perfect alignment on machine teaching algorithm's effectiveness in multi-dimensional tasks (C167-C174). Both evaluations support the differential learning trajectories and dynamic trial adjustment findings, with peer reviewers calling the MT algorithm 'incredibly elegant and important'.

Perfect alignment on the literature-based claim about suboptimal strategies (C180). Both acknowledge the complexity of bias in animal learning, with peer reviewers recognizing that biases can both benefit and hinder learning.

Strong alignment on HABITS system design and technical specifications (C5, C52-C77). OpenEval focuses on technical details while peer reviewers emphasize the system as 'simple yet elegant' and 'robust'. Peer review also includes summary claims C6-C9, C78-C79 not in OpenEval R1.

Strong alignment on multi-modal training capabilities (C97-C104). OpenEval supports these claims with quantitative data. Peer review also includes dynamic foraging claims C105-C107, emphasizing 'complexity of behavioral phenotypes' collectible with the system.

Strong alignment on dataset scale and comprehensiveness (C175-C176). Both evaluations support the unprecedented scale of 200/284 trained mice. Peer reviewers specifically noted 'high n's' as a strength and emphasized the high-throughput nature.

Partial alignment on psychometric performance (C124-C127). OpenEval addresses these specific claims while peer review groups them with additional complex cognitive paradigms (C128-C134), emphasizing overall system capability for 'variety of complex behaviors'.

Partial alignment on temporal weighting analysis (C128-C130). OpenEval evaluates these specific claims while peer review groups them with broader complex cognitive paradigms, accepting them as valid demonstrations of system capabilities.

Partial alignment on confidence-related behavior (C131-C134). OpenEval addresses TI and confidence interpretation while peer review groups these with other complex cognitive paradigms, emphasizing the data are 'strong' and 'convincing'.

Partial alignment on delayed match-to-sample task (C141-C144). OpenEval highlights this as novel implementation in mice. Peer review groups it with other novel paradigms (C145-C156), accepting all as valid demonstrations requiring extended training durations.

Partial alignment on 3-alternative forced choice task (C145-C149). OpenEval evaluates this specific paradigm while peer review groups it with dDMS and context-dependent attention tasks, emphasizing the system's ability to train complex behaviors.

Partial alignment on context-dependent attention task (C150-C156). OpenEval highlights this as challenging novel implementation. Peer review groups it with other novel paradigms, accepting all as demonstrations of 'complexity of behavioral phenotypes' collectible.

Partial alignment on machine teaching algorithm benefits (C10-C12, C178-C183). OpenEval evaluates MT summary claims while peer review groups these with experimental results (C157-C166, C177), calling the algorithm 'incredibly elegant and important'.

Partial alignment on machine teaching vs random training comparison (C157-C160). OpenEval supports findings but notes high failure rate raises calibration questions. Peer review groups with broader MT claims, fully accepting the demonstration of MT's utility.

Partial alignment on differential strategy use between MT and random training (C161-C166). OpenEval supports the sophisticated finding of similar performance but different strategies. Peer review groups with broader MT benefits, emphasizing the algorithm's importance.

Partial alignment on dynamic foraging task (C105-C107). OpenEval evaluates novelty claim with appropriate qualifications. Peer review groups with other multi-modal training demonstrations, emphasizing overall behavioral complexity.

Partial alignment on main contribution summary (C6-C9, C13). OpenEval evaluates these summary claims separately while peer review includes them with system design evaluation, with all reviewers accepting the novelty and significance claims.

Partial alignment on training duration capabilities (C78-C79). OpenEval evaluates these as system capability claims while peer review includes them with overall system design evaluation, accepting the long-duration training capability.

Minimal overlap on novelty claim C177. OpenEval addresses this as part of dataset scale evaluation while peer review mentions it in context of MT algorithm evaluation, both accepting the claim of first real-animal MT implementation.

Minimal overlap on novelty claim C13. OpenEval evaluates this as part of contribution summary while peer review mentions it in context of MT algorithm benefits, both supporting the novelty of the approach.
